text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri welcomes Egyptian President's call for setting up a common Arab market.
-Lebanese Banks Association orders banks to cut the prime rate to 18 percent.
-Banque Audi's shares will begin trading on the Beirut Stock Exchange on January 20.
-President Hrawi expects pressure from Israel on Lebanon and Syria after the Hebron deal with the Palestinians.
-Luxembourg's foreign minister arrives in Beirut for talks on Middle East peace talks.
-Hizbollah (Party of God) urges humanitarian agencies to work for the release of Arab captives languishing in Israeli and allied militia jails.

-An official of the Democratic Front for the Liberation of Palestine (DFLP) denies the group is linked to the recent Katyusha attack on northern Israel as two DFLP members are being interrogated over the incident by Lebanese authorities.
